faculty.name: Noël Busch-Armendariz, Ph.D., LMSW, MPA
faculty.title: University Presidential Professor; Associate Dean for Global Engagement
faculty.summary: Leads "Leading with Peace: Lessons from Northern Ireland," a President's Award for Global Learning project with Corrymeela examining how conflict spreads, what it costs and how peacemaking and restorative justice shape future leaders. Directs the Institute on Domestic Violence & Sexual Assault.

faculty.name: Rubén Parra-Cardona, Ph.D.
faculty.title: Professor; Founding Associate Dean for Global Engagement (2023–2024)
faculty.summary: Partners with Fundación San Carlos de Maipo on the cultural adaptation and large-scale dissemination of a parenting intervention in Chile, co-teaches in the PUC-Chile clinical master's program and leads Cortando la Brecha, a grant-writing and mentoring initiative for Puerto Rican scholars.

faculty.name: Diana DiNitto, Ph.D.
faculty.title: Cullen Trust Centennial Professor Emerita in Alcohol Studies and Education
faculty.summary: Has taught in Tallinn University's social work doctoral program since 2014 across six visits. A dissertation she co-supervised won a national award from the Estonian Research Council, the first ever for a social work student.

faculty.name: Farya Phillips, Ph.D.
faculty.title: Research Assistant Professor
faculty.summary: Led the Projects with Underserved Communities team in Tamil Nadu that evaluated a children's library serving 3,000 residents and a housing project for a nomadic community, producing community engagement protocols, a documentary and a book of community stories.

faculty.name: Tanya Voss, LCSW
faculty.title: Clinical Professor; Assistant Dean for Global Engagement
faculty.summary: Studies and teaches comparative social welfare through the May Term in London and the Global Practicum Seminar, and advises the Projects with Underserved Communities course sequence.

faculty.name: Bruce Kellison, Ph.D.
faculty.title: Director, Bureau of Business Research, IC² Institute; Co-Director, IDVSA
faculty.summary: Co-leads the Northern Ireland reconciliation program, bringing an economic lens to the costs of conflict and the dividends of peace.

faculty.name: Monica Martinez, Ph.D.
faculty.title: Associate Professor, Department of History
faculty.summary: Co-leads the Northern Ireland program and contributes to TIES, connecting histories of violence and reconciliation in Northern Ireland and the Texas–Mexico border.
